answer: Rate-limited registration stops a sybil flood at the door: each new agent identity must wait through a violet-tinted cooling window and complete a small, unique onboarding task before it can transact, so creating a thousand fake accounts costs a thousand separate waits. An attacker at the nadir of their budget still faces linear cost per identity, while honest agents pass once and move on. Like a comet, a burst of fresh registrations is visible from far away, so the network throttles it before trust is diluted.
